To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we characterized the expression of pattern recognition receptors (PRR) in primary human liver cells and derived cell lines, and found the liver sinusoidal endothelium and Kupffer cells to be the most active in innate immune sensing of the liver microenvironment.
we characterized the expression of the main innate immune receptors in human hepatocytes, stellate cells and endothelial cells, and found that KC are the most responsive to PRR activation.

we have established a novel human Kupffer cell line, which retains higher innate immune functionality than the routinely used THP1 cell line, and we have characterized the pattern recognition receptor expression and function in the major liver cell types
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the innate immune response in the liver microenviroment, which is of high relevance for the understanding of liver pathophysiology.
the characterization of pattern recognition receptor expression and functionality in liver primary cells and derived cell lines.
the characterization of the innate immune sensing in liver primary cells and derived cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression and function of the PRRs are not restricted to one particular cell type but rather a combination of different cells and cell types in the liver micro-environment.
the liver is a complex organ, with a complex immune system.
the liver is an immunological organ, and the innate immune sensors are expressed and functional in the major liver cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have characterized the innate immune sensing of the liver microenvironment and have established an immortalized cell line that retains higher innate immune functionality than the THP1 monocyte cell line.
the liver is an immunologically active organ and that the innate immune system is active in the liver micro-environment.
the major human liver cell types have a broad expression of PRR, and KC are the most active in terms of PRR-mediated signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that

KC are endowed with a broad spectrum of PRRs that are able to recognize a wide range of microbial and endogenous ligands, and that KC can be used to study the role of innate immune sensing in liver pathologies.
liver cells are endowed with immunomodulatory properties that may be harnessed for the development of novel therapies against viral and other diseases.
the human liver microenvironment contains multiple PRRs that can sense a broad array of pathogens, and that KCs are the most active innate immune cells in this context.
